title: HEARTS Technical Package for Cardiovascular Disease Management in Primary Health Care
section_heading: HEARTS Technical Package - Total Cardiovascular Risk Stratification
content: The WHO HEARTS technical package emphasizes total cardiovascular risk assessment rather than treating single risk factors in isolation. Cardiovascular risk prediction charts (such as WHO/ISH regional charts for South Asia SEAR D) estimate 10-year risk of a fatal or non-fatal cardiovascular event (myocardial infarction or stroke) based on age, gender, systolic blood pressure, smoking status, and either diabetes status or total blood cholesterol. Risk categories are classified as low (< 10%), moderate (10% to < 20%), high (20% to < 30%), and very high (>= 30%). All patients with established CVD, severe hypertension (SBP >= 160 mmHg), or diabetes with target-organ damage automatically enter the high-risk category without needing chart calculation.

title: HEARTS Technical Package for Cardiovascular Disease Management in Primary Health Care
section_heading: HEARTS Technical Package - Standardized Evidence-Based Treatment Protocols
content: The core components of the HEARTS technical package include: H (Healthy-lifestyle counseling on salt reduction, tobacco cessation, and physical activity); E (Evidence-based treatment protocols emphasizing protocol-driven step-up therapy); A (Access to essential medicines and diagnostics, ensuring continuous availability of core antihypertensive and statin medications); R (Risk-based CVD management focusing resources on high-risk individuals); T (Team-based care utilizing task-sharing with nurses and community health workers); S (Systems for monitoring and program evaluation). Statin therapy is indicated for all individuals with total 10-year CVD risk >= 20% or established clinical atherosclerotic disease.
